official.deadline_note: Two rounds. US citizens resident in the USA apply by 14 October 2026 (applications opened 11 September 2026). All other eligible applicants apply by the Course Funding Deadline in the University Course Directory, which is either 8 December 2026 or 6 January 2027 depending on the course. Applications must be submitted by 11:59pm UK time and all references must be in by the deadline.

official.description: The Gates Cambridge Scholarship is a fully funded postgraduate award for future leaders committed to improving the lives of others, covering the full cost of studying at Cambridge for citizens of any country outside the UK. Around 70 full-cost scholarships are offered each year in any subject, roughly two-thirds to PhD students, and Scholars join a community of about 250 current Scholars and more than 1,700 alumni from 116 countries.
official.program_type: Full-cost postgraduate scholarship at the University of Cambridge

applicant_utility.summary: Gates Cambridge is applied for inside the Cambridge admissions form, so you never write a separate scholarship essay - instead the four published criteria (intellectual ability, reasons for choice of course, commitment to improving lives of others, leadership potential) must be evidenced through your application materials. Check your citizenship first: UK citizens are excluded no matter how strong the profile. Watch the round that applies to you - US applicants resident in the USA face a 14 October 2026 deadline while everyone else answers to their course's funding deadline in December or January - and remember that references must land by the same cut-off, so ask referees at least a month ahead.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Academically outstanding citizens of countries outside the UK pursuing a Cambridge PhD, MLitt or one-year Master's, with a demonstrated commitment to improving the lives of others.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are a citizen of a country outside the UK and that your degree is not on the excluded list (MBA, MASt, PGCE, clinical programmes and the like)
Find your course's exact Course Funding Deadline (8 December 2026 or 6 January 2027) in the University Course Directory
Request references early - they must be submitted by the deadline, with no grace period
Draft evidence for all four selection criteria, especially concrete examples of improving others' lives
Disclose any employer salary or other substantial scholarship before accepting, as the Trust may reduce the maintenance allowance
common_rejection_risks: Missing the 11:59pm UK time cut-off or leaving references outstanding past the deadline
Holding a UK passport, which is a hard exclusion
Applying for an excluded degree (MBA, MFin, PGCE, MASt, most part-time degrees)
Leaving the Gates Cambridge funding section of the combined form incomplete, so the application is treated as admission-only
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Bench fees and scientific equipment costs are excluded and expected to be covered by the Cambridge department; the maintenance allowance is set for a single student, so dependants require the discretionary Dependent Children Allowance (up to £12,793 for one child, £18,244 for two or more, no partner funding).
document_audit: There is no separate scholarship form - every document lives inside the combined admission and funding application
The application is one submission covering course, College and funding; inconsistencies between sections are visible to selectors
alerts: Scholarship offers must be accepted within 72 hours
If you hold a fee award from public authorities such as UKRI you must accept it, and the Trust will not pay or may only share fee and maintenance costs
Departments nominate only the most academically outstanding applicants, so departmental shortlisting comes before Trust selection
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Single combined application through the Cambridge Graduate Application Portal by your round's deadline; academic departments nominate, outcomes follow by early February 2027 (US round) or early April 2027 (international round).

official.deadline_central_display: 2 November 2026 (23:59 UK time); further rounds 11 January 2027 and 1 March 2027
official.deadline_note: Applications are considered at three points in the academic year: 23:59 UK time on 2 November 2026 (award notification by 31 January 2027), 11 January 2027 (notification by 15 April 2027), or 1 March 2027 (notification by 31 May 2027). Departments may also set their own deadline for putting candidates forward.
official.application_cycle: 2027-28 entry; funded start dates 1 August 2027 to 1 November 2027
official.status_note: 50 scholarship places are available; applications are reviewed in a two-stage process by the department and the College Selection Panel.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Each of the 50 scholarships provides full funding for tuition fees for 3.5 years.

Stipend of £27,036 (2027-28 rate) per annum to assist with living costs

Automatic consideration for a standard PhD place if the scholarship is not awarded
eligibility: New PhD applicants only; current registered Imperial PhD students are not eligible

Have made contact with a supervisor in an Imperial academic department who has agreed to supervise the research project
Applications are accepted from candidates from Imperial College London, the UK and worldwide, with no nationality restrictions
The scholarship applies to both full-time and part-time study

Submit the application through the online admissions system; there is no separate scholarship application form
Select the President's PhD Scholarship option in the funding section of the additional questions tab

Research potential - research experience to date, interest in discovery, the research plan and its potential contribution, and the departmental statement

official.application_route: Apply through Imperial's online admissions system, select the President's PhD Scholarship in the funding section, and let your department put you forward.
official.citizenship_residency: No restrictions on nationality; some departments may be unable to support international candidates
official.international_eligibility: Open to applicants from Imperial College London, the UK and worldwide
official.research_requirement: A research proposal forming page 2 of the two-page personal statement; a more detailed research proposal document may be required by the department
official.duration: 3.5 years of funding for a PhD place
official.description: The President's PhD Scholarships provide full funding for tuition fees and a generous stipend for a 3.5-year PhD place at Imperial College London, alongside cohort-building opportunities with other President's PhD Scholars. The scheme has higher than usual eligibility requirements, attracting candidates who show excellent academic performance and promising research potential, and applicants not selected are automatically considered for a standard PhD.
official.program_type: Centrally funded doctoral scholarship scheme for new PhD entrants

verification.notes: Official Imperial College London President's PhD scholarships page fetched in full: £27,036 stipend at the 2027-28 rate, full tuition funding for 3.5 years, £2,000 consumables fund, 50 places, two-stage selection and the three 2026-27 deadlines all verified verbatim.

applicant_utility.summary: The gating item for this scholarship is a supervisor, not a form: you must have an Imperial academic who has agreed to supervise your project before you apply, and each supervisor can support only one President's scholar at a time, so check the Unavailable Supervisors page before you fall in love with a project. Your personal statement has a mandated two-page architecture - page one motivation, page two the research proposal - so treat page two as the real scholarship essay and write it in the first person as encouraged. If your department misses the 2 November 2026 round you still have January and March rounds, but earlier rounds mean earlier notification, so aim for November.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-performing new PhD applicants worldwide holding a first class or equivalent undergraduate/integrated Master's degree (or a Master's distinction) who have already secured a willing supervisor.
application_readiness_checklist: Contact a potential supervisor and get explicit agreement to supervise before starting the application
Check the Unavailable Supervisors page so you do not approach someone already committed to another President's scholar
Select the President's PhD Scholarship in the funding section of the additional questions tab - the default application is admission-only
Build the two-page personal statement deliberately: page 1 motivations, page 2 research proposal
Line up two academic referees who are not your proposed supervisor
common_rejection_risks: Applying without securing supervisor agreement first, or choosing a supervisor who is unavailable for this scheme
Leaving the scholarship option unselected in the funding section, so only admission is assessed
Missing departmental internal deadlines for putting candidates forward
A weak research plan - research potential is assessed through the plan and its potential contribution, not just past grades
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The award covers tuition for 3.5 years plus a £27,036 annual stipend and £2,000 consumables; it does not publish travel or relocation coverage, so flights and settling-in costs remain yours.
document_audit: The two-page personal statement is a hard structure: cramming everything onto page one or letting the proposal spill to page three breaks the format
Referees must be academic and must exclude the proposed supervisor - nominating the supervisor is a self-inflicted rejection
If your department wants more than two pages of proposal detail, use the separate research proposal upload slot
alerts: Current registered Imperial PhD students cannot be considered - the scheme is strictly for new applicants
The Department Special Case route exists for candidates who miss the grade criteria; you must contact the department before applying
Candidates who are not selected are automatically considered for a standard PhD place, so a 'no' on the scholarship is not a 'no' on admission
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Online admissions application with the scholarship selected; department shortlists on academic merit and potential, the College Selection Panel makes the final decision, and outcomes follow between 31 January and 31 May 2027 depending on round.
